# Model Fitting Setup Validation

Make the estimand and fitted data explicit before comparing or accepting
models.

## Setup

Resolve the applicable choices:

- requested output: prediction, optimum location, response at the optimum,
  model metric, coefficient, p-value, class, or another quantity;
- response and predictor definitions, units, transformations, and category or
  event orientation;
- included row scope, controls, baselines, endpoints, missing values, and
  replicate handling;
- candidate models, formulas, fixed parameters, and fitting implementation;
- comparison metric and convention

    def copy_history(self, history_id: str, name: str | None = None, all_datasets: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Create a new history by copying an existing one.

        :type history_id: str
        :param history_id: ID of the history to copy.

        :type name: str
        :param name: Optional name for new history

        :type all_datasets: bool
        :param all_datasets: Whether to copy also deleted datasets and dataset collections.

        :rtype: dict
        :return: Dictionary containing information about the newly created history
        """
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {"source": "history"}
        if name is not None:
            payload["name"] = name
        payload["history_id"] = history_id
        if all_datasets:
            payload["all_datasets"] = all_datasets

        return self._post(payload)

# Galaxy UDT Templates And Troubleshooting

Read only the section needed for the current UDT.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a pinned BioContainer found through one
bounded live BioContainers lookup. Use a bare tagged reference without
`docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  selected-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

python -c 'import base64, pathlib, sys; pathlib.Path("job.py").write_bytes(base64.b64decode(sys.argv[1]))' "$SCRIPT_B64"
python job.py "$(inputs.inpu

representation.name: BMI-only PR Logistic Regression AIC
representation.shell_command:
set -eu
cat > fit.R <<'RSCRIPT'
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
if (length(args) != 1L) stop("Expected exactly one tabular input")
stopifnot(is.function(stats::glm))
dat0 <- utils::read.delim(
  args[[1]],
  header = TRUE,
  sep = "\t",
  quote = "",
  comment.char = "",
  check.names = FALSE,
  na.strings = c("", "NA", "NaN")
)
needed <- c("Efficacy", "BMI")
if (!all(needed %in% names(dat0))) {
  stop(paste("Required columns missing:", paste(setdiff(needed, names(dat0)), collapse = ", ")))
}
eff <- trimws(as.character(dat0[["Efficacy"]]))
bmi <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(dat0[["BMI"]])))
keep <- !is.na(eff) & nzchar(eff) & !is.na(bmi)
dat <- data.frame(
  PR = as.integer(eff[keep] == "PR"),
  BMI = bmi[keep]
)
if (nrow(dat) == 0L) stop("No complete Efficacy/BMI observations")
if (length(unique(dat$PR)) != 2L) stop("PR indicator does not contain both classes")
fit <- stats::glm(PR ~ BMI, data = dat, family = stats::binomial(link = "logit"))
aic <- as.numeric(stats::AIC(fit))
out <- data.frame(
  metric = c("AIC", "n_complete", "n_PR", "formula", "family", "response_event", "predictor"),
  value = c(
    format(aic, digits = 17, scientific = TRUE),
    as.character(nrow(dat)),
    as.character(sum(dat$PR == 1L)),
    "PR ~ BMI",
    "binomial(link=logit)",
    "Efficacy == PR",
    "BMI"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
utils::write.table(out, file = "result.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
RSCRIPT
Rscript fit.R "$(inputs.input.path)"
